name: Popliteofibular ligament
description: Short, strong band from the popliteus musculotendinous junction to the fibular styloid, a primary posterolateral corner stabilizer with the LCL and popliteus tendon. A thin low-signal band about 1 cm long and 1–2 mm thick, best on coronal oblique or 3D images.
variants_pitfalls: Present in nearly all knees at dissection, but routine 2D MRI often misses it (8–38% on standard coronal or routine studies, 53–71% on coronal oblique, 91% on 3D). Not seeing it on routine 2D images is normal.
MRI is unreliable for the ligament itself (68% accuracy against surgery), so lean on indirect signs: popliteus junction edema, styloid edema or avulsion, and LCL or popliteus tendon injury.
A small horizontal styloid tip avulsion (arcuate sign) points to popliteofibular and arcuate injury; a larger lateral fibular head fragment carries the LCL and biceps.
Bifurcated or double forms occur (about 16% of cadaver limbs), so two thin bands near the styloid can be normal.
